name: Emperor Zhang of Han
wd_description: Emperor of the Chinese Han Dynasty (AD 56 – 88) (ruled 75 – 88)
extract:
Emperor Zhang of Han (Chinese: 漢章帝; pinyin: Hàn Zhāngdì; Wade–Giles: Han Chang-ti; 56 – 9 April 88), born Liu Da (劉炟), was an emperor of the Chinese Han dynasty from 75 to 88. He was the third emperor of the Eastern Han.
Emperor Zhang was a hard-working and diligent emperor. He reduced taxes and paid close attention to all affairs of state. Zhang also reduced government spending as well as promoted Confucianism. As a result, Han society prospered and its culture flourished during this period. Along with his father Emperor Ming, Emperor Zhang's reign has been highly praised and was regarded as the golden age of the Eastern Han period, and their reigns are collectively known as the Rule of Ming and Zhang. 
He was also greatly influenced by the women around him. At first, he consulted his stepmother and foster mother, Empress Dowager Ma, in governing state affairs, and there was a strong and effective cooperation between them. The emperor was highly diligent and dutiful in fulfilling his filial obligations toward her. After her death, Emperor Zhang showed great favor toward his wife, Empress Dou, and to some extent came under her influence in political affairs. He also elevated her family to the highest positions of power within the palace, keeping them close to himself. This form of favoritism resembled nepotism, which went against the ideals of his father and grandfather, and especially contradicted the administrative principles established by Empress Dowager Ma.
During his reign, Chinese troops under the leadership of General Ban Chao progressed far west while in pursuit of Xiongnu insurgents harassing the trade routes now collectively known as the Silk Road.
The Eastern Han dynasty, after Emperor Zhang, would be plagued with internal strife between royal factions and eunuchs struggling for power.  The people for the coming century and a half would yearn for the good days of Emperors Ming and Zhang. The strife between the eunuchs and royal factions would start a chain reaction of events that led to the end of the Han dynasty in 220.
